title: Fleet Orchestrator: operator undo/redo + guided scaling playbooks in Console
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Enable operators to apply, preview, and revert fleet-level scaling decisions with low cognitive load. This work adds an undo/redo affordance to the Fleet Orchestrator UI, couples that with templated scaling playbooks (guided suggestions for autoscale rules and throughput guarantees), and surfaces change history and impact estimates in the Console. Goal is to reduce manual mistakes when adjusting dedicated capacity and to make rollbacks fast and auditable.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can apply a scaling playbook from a curated list and see a 60s simulation of expected throughput/latency change before committing
Every change to Autoscale rules or instance counts is recorded as a reversible entry in the Fleet change history with user, timestamp, reason, and before/after diffs
Undo (single-step) and Redo are available for the last 10 operator actions on a fleet; undo performs a safe revert that validates resource availability and surfaces errors
Change history supports filtering by operator, time range, and change type, and exposes links to related GitHub PRs and rollout notes
Backend exposes an audit events API used by Console; no plaintext secrets or keys are included in audit payloads
Telemetry events emitted for apply/undo/redo/playbook-preview are instrumented for cost/latency impact analysis
tasks: Design: finalize mockups for playbook picker, preview simulator, and undo snackbar (DES-2037)
Frontend: implement playbook picker, preview modal, undo/redo controls, and history timeline component (ENG-21450)
Backend: create change-event model, safe-revert operation, and audit API endpoints (ENG-19234)
SLO/Policy: define constraints for automatic safeguards (e.g., cannot scale below committed capacity) and validate in simulator
Integration tests: end-to-end test applying + undoing a change with mock dedicated pools
Runbook: update operator-runbooks and incident playbooks to include undo/redo guidance
decisions: Use optimistic client-side preview for playbook impact estimates using historical throughput curves; final commit will run server-side validation
Limit undo history to 10 actions per-fleet to bound storage and UI complexity
Implement undo as a declarative 'apply previous desired state' operation rather than inverse operations to avoid drift
Playbooks will be versioned and editable by admins; initial set curated by Product and SRE
open_questions: How should playbook suggestions be ranked for multi-tenant fleets with varying SLAs? (product + SRE decision)
If an undo fails due to capacity constraints during revert, should we queue a rollback or surface a forced rollback that requires approval?
Should undo operations be allowed across model-version rollouts, or blocked when the previous variant is incompatible?
What retention window is appropriate for change history to balance auditability vs. storage cost?
